title: Am falschen Weg
setting: A meadow with no path in it, no signal, and a dog barking somewhere below.

options.es: Grüezi. Entschuldigung, können Sie mir helfen?
options.en: Hello. Excuse me, can you help me?
options.feedback: Greet first, then ask. Können Sie mir is the polite opening and it costs you two words.
No greeting and no können Sie. It is understood and it lands like an instruction.
Grüezi, not hallo. And you do not have a problem, you have a wrong turning.

steps.speaker: Frau mit Hunden
steps.en: Where do you want to get to?

options.feedback: Sich verlaufen, and the sich is not optional. Saying it plainly is faster than explaining the route.
Ich habe mich verlaufen. Without the sich it is not a sentence anybody says.

options.es: Zur Hütte. Aber ich finde den Weg nicht.
options.en: To the hut. But I cannot find the path.
options.feedback: Answers her question and states the problem. She asked where to, so tell her where to.

steps.speaker: Frau mit Hunden
steps.es: Ah. Sie sind zu weit links.
steps.en: Ah. You are too far to the left.

options.feedback: The useful question. Twenty minutes, and she is about to offer to walk them with you.
She will wave it away. A lot of people do it there, which is exactly what she says next.
The sign was not wrong. There were three paths and two names and you picked on looks.

steps.speaker: Frau mit Hunden
steps.es: Ich gehe auch dorthin. Kommen Sie.
steps.en: I am going there too. Come along.

options.feedback: She is not going there. You will work that out twenty minutes later, at the sign, when she turns round.
You will not, and refusing help on a mountain is the one place where politeness is the wrong instinct.
Fine, and it is more words than the moment needs. She already decided.
